brief.headline: Push for ₹66.48/KG (the best price we already pay elsewhere) to save ₹1.26 Cr a year.

priceAsk.summary: Ask them to match ₹66.48/KG — the price Sayaji Industries Limited gives us for the same Dextrose.
priceAsk.basis: We currently pay them ₹68.45/KG, which is 3.0% above the ₹66.48/KG we pay Sayaji. The open market typical band for Anhydrous Dextrose IP is ₹66–73/kg, so ₹66.48/KG sits at the bottom of that range — fair and achievable. Closing this gap saves us ₹1.26 Cr every year.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Keep the current 30 Days After Receipt terms; no change needed.

brief.financialLeverage: Gujarat Ambuja is healthy: they bring in ₹5995.63 Cr in sales and keep 8.5% of every rupee as profit, with low debt (0.13x). We are tiny to them — our ₹21.21 Cr spend is just 0.35% of their revenue. That means they don't need us badly, so we can't squeeze hard on relationship alone. Instead, lean on the fact that we already pay less elsewhere and that we're lining up second sources — they'll see we have options and will walk if the price stays high.

evidence.point: We pay them 3.0% more than our best price
Closing that gap saves ₹1.26 Cr per year
They keep a comfortable 8.5% profit and have strong operating margin of 11.7%
Our spend is only 0.35% of their ₹5995.63 Cr revenue
Market asking price band for Anhydrous Dextrose IP is ₹60–81/kg, typically ₹66–73/kg

alternates.name: Gulshan Polyols Ltd (a lead to qualify — verify before RFQ)
alternates.why: Listed starch & polyol maker with ₹2359.06 Cr revenue, health score B (62/100) — described as a drop-in alternate to Gujarat Ambuja; stronger financials than our current supplier.

alternates.name: Sanstar Ltd (a lead to qualify — verify before RFQ)
alternates.why: Recently-listed maize-derivatives specialist making starch and dextrose, ₹821.13 Cr revenue, health score C (57/100) — growing capacity.

alternates.name: Roquette India Pvt Ltd (a lead to qualify — verify before RFQ)
alternates.why: Indian arm of global starch major with ₹2898.05 Cr revenue — pharma-grade dextrose and excipients; premium quality and very reliable, though health score is D (28/100).

risks: Gujarat Ambuja supplies 56% of our Dextrose (₹21.21 Cr) — we are heavily dependent on them, so pushing too hard without a qualified backup in place could leave us exposed if they walk away.
We are only 0.35% of their business, so they won't fight to keep us — the price ask must be justified by market evidence and our own data, not by threatening to leave.
The alternates listed are leads from public research, not yet qualified or priced — we need to start technical and commercial qualification now so we have real leverage in 60–90 days.
Their health score is C (55/100), middling but not distressed — they're stable enough that a reasonable ask won't tip them, but not so weak that we can lean on desperation.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but we're paying you ₹68.45/KG when we already get the same Dextrose at ₹66.48/KG from Sayaji — can we talk about moving to that price?
